program_name: Bioengineering for Personalized Medicine (B4PM) - Master's Degree / Laurea Magistrale in Bioengineering for Personalized Medicine (Italian institutional wording also uses 'Bioingegneria per la Medicina Personalizzata'). Inter-university (interateneo) degree jointly established by the University of Trento, the University of Verona and the University of Modena and Reggio Emilia, with the University of Trento - Department of Industrial Engineering (DII) as the administrative seat.
teaching_language: Fully English. The official programme page states 'LANGUAGE: English' and describes it as 'A fully English-taught programme with students from around the world'. There is no Italian-language percorso and no mixed English/Italian track. Art. 24 c.3 of the teaching regulations requires the final thesis to be written and defended in English. IMPORTANT NUANCE: although teaching is entirely in English, the teaching regulations (Art. 12 h and the notes to the study plan table) impose an ITALIAN language requirement DURING the degree - 'La conoscenza della lingua italiana pari al livello A1-CEFR e richiesta per poter sostenere gli esami del secondo anno di corso' (knowledge of Italian at CEFR A1 level is required in order to sit the second-year examinations); passing this check awards the 3 CFU of 'Altre attivita formative' (other training activities). Italian A1 is therefore NOT an admission requirement but is a progression requirement in the second year.
campus: Rovereto - Polo Tecnologico di Rovereto (Polo Meccatronica), via Fortunato Zeni 8, Building C, staircase D, 38068 Rovereto (Trento), Italy. This is the address given both on the official programme page ('LOCATION: Polo Tecnologico Rovereto') and in Art. 1 c.4 of the teaching regulations ('Le attivita didattiche si svolgono presso la sede dell'Universita di Trento a Rovereto c/o Polo Meccatronica, via Fortunato Zeni, 8'). Being an inter-university degree with Verona and Modena and Reggio Emilia, part of the teaching staff comes from those universities and students may attend courses offered by the partner universities (Art. 11 of the regulations allows elective courses to be chosen from all consortium universities), but the administrative and main teaching seat is Rovereto. [uncertain - the orienta.unitn.it page for this programme instead states 'Sede: Dipartimento di Ingegneria Industriale, Povo - Trento', which conflicts with the programme page and the regulations; the orienta page also links to the Mechatronics Engineering admission page, so it appears to contain template errors. Rovereto is the correct location.]
degree_class: LM-21 (Ingegneria Biomedica / Biomedical Engineering). The 2026/2027 admission call heads the programme as 'Bioengineering for Personalized Medicine (classe LM-21 R)' - the 'R' suffix denotes the renewed Italian degree class. Art. 1 c.1 of the 2024 teaching regulations states the programme belongs to class 'LM-21 - Classe delle lauree magistrali in Ingegneria Biomedica' (DD.MM. 16 March 2007). Duration 2 years, 120 ECTS. Esse3/CINECA course code 0347H.
admission_type:
TWO DIFFERENT REGIMES depending on citizenship/residence:
(1) EUROPEANS AND EQUIVALENTS (including non-EU citizens legally resident in Italy with a qualifying stay permit): OPEN / FREE ACCESS with verification of admission requirements ('ACCESS: Free' on the programme page; 'The programme is free access to Europeans and Equivalents: to be admitted, admission requirements must be verified'). There is no numero programmato, no ranking and no competitive selection for this group - an application for requirement verification must nevertheless be submitted online in the May-November window, and the outcome arrives by email within one month.
(2) NON-EUROPEAN CITIZENS LIVING OUTSIDE ITALY: RESTRICTED, competitive selection call ('selection call based on academic curriculum and merit') with a reserved quota of 25 places, a single deadline, an application fee, a merit ranking and a 50/100 eligibility threshold. This route is governed by the joint DII call for admission (Annex 17 to the Rectoral Decree) covering the four English-taught DII master's degrees.
There is NO TOLC, NO SAT and no written entrance examination in either route.
academic_requirements:
QUALIFICATION (both routes): a Bachelor's degree of at least 3 years, or another qualification obtained abroad and recognised as suitable ('titolo di laurea conseguito all'estero riconosciuto idoneo'). No enrolment with educational debts (debiti formativi / OFA) is permitted - Art. 3 c.1 of the teaching regulations.

CURRICULAR REQUIREMENTS (Art. 3 c.2 of the teaching regulations, Table A - applied to the Europeans/equivalents route and used as the reference for foreign degrees):
(a) Holders of an Italian Bachelor's degree in class L-8 (Information Engineering) or L-9 (Industrial Engineering) AUTOMATICALLY meet the curricular requirements.
(b) Holders of an Italian degree in any other class must have earned at least 75 ECTS across the SSD groups of Table A, and ALL THREE thresholds must be met:
  - at least 24 ECTS in MAT/02 Algebra, MAT/03 Geometry, MAT/05 Mathematical analysis, MAT/06 Probability and mathematical statistics, MAT/07 Mathematical physics, MAT/08 Numerical analysis, SECS-S/01 Statistics, SECS-S/02 Statistics for experimental and technological research, SECS-S/06 Mathematical methods of economics, finance and actuarial sciences;
  - at least 15 ECTS in FIS/01 Experimental physics, FIS/03 Physics of matter, FIS/07 Applied physics, CHIM/03 General and inorganic chemistry, CHIM/06 Organic chemistry, CHIM/07 Chemical foundations of technologies;
  - at least 36 ECTS in ING-IND/06, ING-IND/08, ING-IND/09, ING-IND/10, ING-IND/11, ING-IND/12, ING-IND/13, ING-IND/14, ING-IND/15, ING-IND/21, ING-IND/22, ING-IND/23, ING-IND/31, ING-IND/32, ING-IND/34 Industrial bioengineering, ING-IND/35, ING-INF/01 Electronics, ING-INF/02, ING-INF/03, ING-INF/04, ING-INF/05, ING-INF/06 Electronic and informatics bioengineering, ING-INF/07, ICAR/01 Hydraulics, ICAR/08 Structural mechanics, SECS-P/08 Management.
(c) Holders of a foreign degree: curricular requirements are verified by a Committee appointed by the Departmental Council on the proposal of the Programme Board, on the basis of appropriate equivalences between the contents of the examinations already taken and the disciplinary fields of Table A. Applicants under (a) and (c) who lack some requirements are told by the Committee which missing credits must be acquired BEFORE the personal-preparation check, because enrolment with debts is not allowed.

PERSONAL PREPARATION (Art. 3 c.3): mandatory verification. It is considered ADEQUATE for graduates whose weighted average mark in the examinations taken for the first-cycle degree (excluding the final project) is NOT LOWER THAN 23/30 (in the average, 30 cum laude counts as 31/30). For candidates with a foreign qualification the adequacy check may also be carried out by means of a TEST before a committee appointed by the Departmental Council, in the manner set out in the admission call.

NON-EU SELECTION ROUTE (a.y. 2026/2027 call, Art. 1-2 and 4): 25 places reserved for non-European citizens living outside Italy across this programme (the same call also assigns 25 places each to Materials Engineering, Mechatronics Engineering and Management and Industrial Systems Engineering). Degree obtained or obtainable by 30 June 2026 (31 October 2026 for non-Europeans graduating at an Italian university holding a valid Italian study stay permit). Accepted qualifications: Bachelor's degree in Industrial Engineering (class L-9) OR in Information Engineering (class L-8) awarded in Italy in compliance with the programme regulations, or a degree obtained abroad recognised as suitable. Weighted average of at least 23/30 (for foreign degrees the GPA is considered according to the country of graduation). Scoring out of 100 points: (a) coherence between the previous degree and the objectives of the master - max 30 points; (b) curriculum studiorum (performance and evaluations in previous studies, any post-graduate courses, other extra-academic activities) - max 60 points; (c) additional language skills (English above B2 or knowledge of other languages) - max 10 points. Candidates scoring 50/100 or above are eligible; ties are broken in favour of the younger candidate. The Selection Committee is appointed by rectoral decree and, per the BINDING Italian text, consists of at least 3 professors of the Department of Industrial Engineering (DII); it may meet online and may require an interview if the uploaded documents do not allow an adequate assessment. [uncertain - the English courtesy translation wrongly says the committee is drawn from the Department of Information Engineering and Computer Science (DISI); the Italian binding version says DII.]

ACTUAL 2026/2027 NON-EU OUTCOME (ranking published 13 May 2026): 25 positions available, 2 scholarships available; 15 candidates admitted (scores from 100/100 down to 57.5/100, the top two with scholarship), 3 candidates scored below 50 and were not admitted, and 24 further applicants were declared not eligible. The quota was therefore not filled.

FEES (non-EU citizens living abroad, merit-based): maximum EUR 6,000 per academic year - tuition waiver for a score of 90-100/100, EUR 1,000 for 70-89.99/100, EUR 2,000 for 60-69.99/100, EUR 4,500 for 50-59.99/100. Second-year fees depend on ECTS earned by 10 August 2027: waiver for 42 or more ECTS, EUR 1,000 for 36-41, EUR 2,000 for 24-35, EUR 4,500 for 6-23, EUR 6,000 for fewer than 6. Scholarships: non-European candidates at the top of the ranking scoring at least 70/100 may be awarded one; no separate application is needed; holders are exempt from tuition fees; it is a partial contribution to stay costs paid only after actual arrival in Italy, renewable for the second year on merit, and not compatible with MAECI, Universita a colori-Unicolor or Invest your Talent in Italy scholarships. For Europeans and equivalents, tuition is income-based (ISEE) under the general UniTrento fee rules.
language_requirements:
ENGLISH - B2 (CEFR) is mandatory for admission in both routes.

Non-EU selection route (binding call, Art. 2 B): full B2 level (4 skills) must be attested BY THE APPLICATION DEADLINE (4 March 2026) by one of: (i) a certificate issued by an internationally recognised body; (ii) a declaration issued by the institution that awarded the first- or second-cycle degree certifying that the entire programme was officially taught in English; (iii) having passed a certifiable English examination at B2 level or higher within one's own university study path, provided all four language skills were assessed; (iv) declaring in the online application that one holds the citizenship of a country whose official language is English. The corsi.unitn.it non-EU page adds a self-declaration of having graduated in an English-speaking country.

Europeans and equivalents route: English at least B2 CEFR, proved by (i) having passed a university exam in English at B2 as part of the degree programme, or (ii) a language certificate recognised by UniTrento (list at https://www.cla.unitn.it/node/780). If neither is available, the requirement can be made up by taking and passing the English test at the University Language Centre (Centro Linguistico di Ateneo, CLA) BEFORE enrolment; the written part is held in person in Trento at the CLA and the speaking part is online. Six CLA sessions published for Master's admission in 2026 - Session 1: registration 27 March to 20 April 12:00 CET, written 27 April 14:30, speaking 8 May; Session 2: registration 20 April to 15 May, written 25 May 14:30, speaking 5 June; Session 3: registration 16 May to 25 June, written 6 July 14:30, speaking 17 July; Session 4: registration 26 June to 21 August, written 2 September 14:30, speaking 11 September; Session 5: registration 24 August to 2 October, written 12 October 14:30, speaking 23 October; Session 6: registration 5 October to 13 November, written 23 November 14:30, speaking 4 December. Registration for the CLA test: https://webapps.unitn.it/Apply/en/Web/GoHome/ammissione/ENAdm_STA26 . After achieving the language requirement the candidate must email the Student Support Service to proceed with enrolment. Art. 3 c.3 d) of the teaching regulations also allows self-certification of having passed the English test of the CLA of UniTrento or of another university.

ITALIAN - not required for admission, but required during the programme: students whose mother tongue is not Italian must reach CEFR A1 Italian in order to sit the SECOND-YEAR examinations; passing this check awards the 3 CFU of 'other training activities'. The credits can also be awarded directly to students holding a suitable certificate of an equivalent or higher level recognised by the Department or by the CLA; the test is delivered by CLA language experts.
required_documents:
NON-EU SELECTION ROUTE (Art. 3 c.6 of the call, plus the corsi.unitn.it non-EU page). An official translation into English (or Italian) is required for any document not issued in English or Italian; illegible documents are not considered and incomplete or unsubmitted applications are excluded:
1. Copy of a valid passport (only the pages with photo and personal data).
2. Curriculum vitae et studiorum in English, preferably in the European/Europass format (https://europass.europa.eu).
3. Copy of the Bachelor's degree certificate if already awarded, or a certificate of enrolment stating the expected graduation date. Full information on the grading scale is required, otherwise the application is not considered. Graduates of Italian universities submit a self-declaration under D.P.R. 445/2000; UniTrento students/graduates do not upload this document.
4. Transcript of academic records listing all courses, examinations and marks (final-year candidates must also list examinations not yet passed), including the weighted average mark and the minimum-to-maximum range of marks. Same self-declaration rule for Italian universities.
5. English language qualification / proof of B2 (certificate, university declaration, certified B2 exam or citizenship declaration).
Application fee EUR 30.00 per application, to be paid by the deadline (a separate application must be submitted, and a separate fee paid, for each master's degree applied for); non-payment means exclusion. Admitted candidates then pay a non-refundable enrolment confirmation fee of EUR 100.00 within the deadline stated in or communicated with the ranking; failure to confirm counts as renunciation and the place goes to the next candidate in the ranking. Confirmed candidates must pre-enrol on the Universitaly portal at the competent Italian diplomatic mission (mandatory to obtain the visa and to receive the UniTrento admission letter) and apply for a study visa. UniTrento may request a statement of verification and/or statement of comparability; foreign degrees are verified only after the admission and pre-enrolment procedure is complete.

EUROPEANS AND EQUIVALENTS ROUTE: an online application for verification of the admission requirements must be submitted by all applicants, including students already enrolled at UniTrento and those who already meet all requirements; it can be submitted before graduating or before completing the curricular requirements. Applicants who studied at another university must attach a self-declaration of the examinations taken, indicating for each examination: the Scientific Disciplinary Sector (SSD), the credits (CFU), the date it was taken, the final mark, and the syllabus (detailed course programme). Proof of English B2 (university exam or recognised certificate) is required, or the CLA test must be passed before enrolment. No application fee is stated on the official page for this route.
entry_exam_or_test: No entrance examination. There is no TOLC, no SAT and no written admission test. For non-Europeans, selection is entirely document-based (100-point scoring of qualifications); an INTERVIEW is not a standard step and is requested only when the documentation attached to the online application does not allow the Selection Committee to assess the candidature adequately (Art. 4 c.4 of the call). For Europeans and equivalents, admission is by verification of the curricular requirements only; however, Art. 3 c.3 c) of the teaching regulations - echoed on the corsi.unitn.it EU page ('the verification of the adequacy of personal background may also include a test before a committee appointed by the Departmental Council') - allows a personal-preparation TEST before a committee for candidates holding a foreign degree recognised as suitable. Personal preparation is considered adequate without further checks for graduates with a weighted average of at least 23/30. The only other test any applicant may have to sit is the English language test at the CLA, and only for candidates who cannot otherwise document B2 English; and, after enrolment, the Italian A1 test needed to sit second-year examinations.
application_deadline_eu: Academic year 2026/2027, Europeans and equivalents (free access with verification of requirements): applications open from 18 MAY 2026 to 12 NOVEMBER 2026. The corsi.unitn.it admission page states 'When: from May 18 to November 12 2026' and the programme homepage banner confirms 'Application request for 2026/2027 is open until November 12 2026'. All applicants must apply, including students already enrolled at UniTrento and those who already meet all the requirements; the application may be submitted before graduating or before completing the curricular requirements. Outcome: an email within one month of submitting the application (rolling processing, no ranking). Online application: https://webapps.unitn.it/Apply/en/Web/GoHome/ammissione/ammdii26 (verified live, HTTP 200). No application fee is indicated for this route on the official page. English B2 must be documented, or made up through the CLA test before enrolment (last CLA session of 2026: written 23 November, speaking 4 December).
application_deadline_non_eu: Academic year 2026/2027, non-European citizens living outside Italy (competitive call, 25 reserved places): application deadline 4 MARCH 2026 at 12:00 CET (both the binding Italian call, Art. 3 c.2 'La scadenza per la candidatura e il 4 marzo 2026 alle ore 12.00 (CET)', and the corsi.unitn.it non-EU page agree). The EUR 30.00 application fee must be paid by the same deadline. Rankings: by 20 May 2026 (actually published on 13 May 2026). Confirmation and payment of the EUR 100.00 confirmation fee: within the deadline communicated by UniTrento staff / stated in the ranking. Pre-enrolment on Universitaly: within 2 weeks from confirmation. Visa: before enrolment - only candidates who obtained the Italian entry visa no later than 31 October 2026 are admitted, otherwise admission lapses. Bachelor's degree graduation: by 30 June 2026 for non-Europeans graduating outside Italy (by 31 October 2026 for non-Europeans graduating in Italy with a valid study stay permit). Arrival in Trento: all international students must arrive by 31 October 2026 and must be present for the start of classes; lessons take place only in person. As of 31 August 2026 this session is closed and the ranking has been published.

uncertainty_notes:
1) INTER-UNIVERSITY (INTERATENEO) DEGREE - CONFIRMED. The task note that the programme is shared with Verona and Modena-Reggio Emilia is correct and officially documented: Art. 1 c.2 of the teaching regulations describes the programme as 'interateneo Universita di Trento, Universita di Verona ed Universita di Modena e Reggio Emilia', with the DII of the University of Trento as the reference teaching structure, and Art. 1 c.3 establishes a joint Collegio Didattico under a Convention signed by the three universities. The orienta.unitn.it page repeats this. However, the official pages do NOT state whether the final award is a single joint degree certificate issued by the three universities or a UniTrento degree with partner involvement; the admission procedure, the fees, the calls, the ranking and the enrolment are all handled exclusively by the University of Trento, and no separate Verona or Modena admission route was found. Applicants should assume they apply to and enrol at UniTrento only. Note also that Art. 11 of the regulations lets students choose elective courses from the offer of all consortium universities, so some teaching may physically take place at partner sites.

2) TWO DIFFERENT ACCESS REGIMES - EASY TO MISREAD. The programme page label 'ACCESS: Free' applies ONLY to Europeans and equivalents. Non-European citizens living outside Italy face a genuinely competitive, capped procedure (25 places, 100-point scoring, 50/100 threshold, published ranking). In 2026/2027, 24 of 42 applicants were declared not eligible and 3 more scored below the threshold, so the practical selectivity for non-EU applicants is high even though the quota was not filled.

3) ENGLISH COURTESY TRANSLATION CONTAINS ERRORS. (a) Art. 4 c.3 of the English PDF says the Selection Committee is drawn from 'the Department of Information Engineering and Computer Science (DISI)'; the binding Italian says 'almeno 3 docenti del Dipartimento di Ingegneria Industriale' (DII). The Italian prevails. (b) The English Art. 2 adds that a foreign qualification must be 'in the fieled [sic] of Information Engineering and Computer Science', whereas the Italian simply requires 'titolo di laurea conseguito all'estero riconosciuto idoneo' assessed against the programme regulations - the English wording appears copied from a DISI call and is narrower than the binding text. (c) The English Art. 7 c.1 Italian counterpart contains a typo: 'euro 6.000,00 (diecimila)' - the figure 6,000 is correct, the spelled-out 'diecimila' (ten thousand) is a leftover from another call. These points are flagged in the relevant fields.

4) TEACHING REGULATIONS VERSION. The only Programme Regulations published on the official documents page are the 2024 ones (Rectoral Decree n. 863 of 23 July 2024, applicable from a.y. 2024/2025). The 2026/2027 educational-offer sheet, however, is headed 'Didactic Regulation 2024 & 2026' and was approved by the Department Board on 18 February 2026, which implies that a 2026 version of the regulations exists but has not been posted on the programme's document page. The curricular requirements reported here are therefore those of the 2024 regulations, and they are consistent with what the live corsi.unitn.it admission page currently publishes (75 ECTS / 24+15+36 thresholds), so the risk of divergence is low but not zero. [uncertain]

5) CURRICULA FOR 2026/2027. The programme page still advertises two curricula - 'Digital Healthcare' and 'Emerging and Sustainable Medical Technologies'. But on the documents page only ONE educational-offer sheet exists for 2026/2027 (filename 'digital-healthcare-26-27'), while 2024/2025 and 2025/2026 each have two. The 2026/2027 sheet in fact contains a single unified 120-ECTS study plan with two elective slots (12a and 12b) offering courses drawn from both former curricula. It is therefore unclear whether the two curricula are still formally separate in 2026/2027 or have been merged into one plan with elective tracks. [uncertain]

6) CAMPUS DISCREPANCY. The programme page and the teaching regulations both place teaching at Rovereto (Polo Tecnologico / Polo Meccatronica, via Fortunato Zeni 8). The orienta.unitn.it page for this same programme states 'Sede: Dipartimento di Ingegneria Industriale, Povo - Trento' and links its 'verifica dei requisiti' to the MECHATRONICS Engineering admission page - both look like template errors on the orientation site. Rovereto is reported as the campus. Note the DII department itself is headquartered in Trento (Povo/Mesiano), which may explain the confusion.

7) ITALIAN LANGUAGE OBLIGATION IS OFTEN OVERLOOKED. Although this is a fully English-taught degree with no Italian requirement at admission, non-Italian-speaking students cannot sit SECOND-YEAR examinations until they demonstrate Italian at CEFR A1 (worth the 3 CFU of 'other activities'). This is stated only in the teaching regulations, not on the admission webpages, and is a real progression condition for international students.

8) EU ROUTE - NO PUBLISHED APPLICATION FEE OR RANKING. The Europeans-and-equivalents page states no application fee, no seat cap and no ranking; the outcome is an individual email within one month. No official page was found confirming the exact EU/ISEE-based tuition band for this specific programme; the general UniTrento EU tuition rules apply and only the general fee pages are linked here. Third-party aggregators quote an EUR 340-3,400 EU range, but that figure comes from the retired offertaformativa.unitn.it site and from commercial portals and was not used.

9) SHARED CALL. The non-EU admission call is not programme-specific: it is Annex 17 to the Rectoral Decree and covers all four English-taught DII master's degrees (Management and Industrial Systems Engineering LM-31 R, Materials Engineering LM-53 R, Mechatronics Engineering LM-33 R, Bioengineering for Personalized Medicine LM-21 R). Candidates may apply to more than one, but must submit and pay for a separate application for each. Unlike the other three programmes, the 25 places for Bioengineering for Personalized Medicine include no EIT-programme reservations.

10) WAF/ACCESS LIMITATION. corsi.unitn.it, www.unitn.it and orienta.unitn.it sit behind an AWS WAF that returns HTTP 405 on direct fetches; the CAPTCHA was deliberately not bypassed. All corsi.unitn.it pages and PDFs cited above were retrieved through a public read-only text-extraction proxy that renders the same public pages, so the content is the live official text but was not read from a direct browser session. webapps.unitn.it was reached directly: the EU application endpoint 'ammdii26' returns HTTP 200 and is live but login-gated, so in-portal dates could not be cross-checked. offertaformativa.unitn.it (the older programme site still referenced inside the 2024 regulations) was not used as a source.

11) CYCLE STATUS AS OF 31 AUGUST 2026. The non-EU session for a.y. 2026/2027 is closed (deadline 4 March 2026, ranking published 13 May 2026). The EU/equivalents window is still OPEN until 12 November 2026. Applicants targeting a.y. 2027/2028 should expect an equivalent non-EU DII call to be published around December 2026 with a deadline in early March 2027.
